name: Vietnamese hát xoan
lineage: Vietnamese hát xoan ancestral-spring-ritual song tradition of Phú Thọ province, the heartland of the Hùng-Kings legendary first-Vietnamese-dynasty mythos. Performance occurs at the Hùng-Kings temple (Đền Hùng) and adjacent communal-house đình precincts during the lunar new-year and Hùng-Kings death-anniversary festivals (lunar tenth day of third month). Three movement types: thờ (worship, slow ceremonial-cadence verse for ancestor-veneration), quả cách (formal-narrative cyclical sections, fourteen canonical pieces), and hội (festival, faster celebratory cadence with audience-participation call-and-response). Performance configuration: a male choir of phường xoan villagers from one of four canonical guild-villages (An Thái, Phù Đức, Kim Đới, Thét), accompanied by phách bamboo clapper and trống cơm small barrel-drum. Modal vocabulary draws on Vietnamese pentatonic with mode-specific cadential conventions. The tradition was nearly extinct by the 1990s, but systematic transmission-revival has since spread across the four guild-villages. Distinguished from quan họ by xoan's ritual-ancestor-veneration (vs courtship-festival) functional framing; distinguished from ca trù by xoan's village-collective-male-choir (vs chamber-female-soloist) ensemble configuration.
